title: Context Lens Portal + Session Jumpflow: Sidebar & Routing Reframe
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: As teams scale across multiple projects and deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), users frequently lose context when switching between model routes, rollout stages and cost views. Current left-nav is dense and forces users to either drill deep or open multiple tabs. Goal: design a lightweight, discoverable "Context Lens" that surfaces session-scoped context (active workspace, route, rollout, cost lens) in a compact portal attached to the left dock and a fast keyboard-driven 'Session Jump' flow. The work covers IA changes (route grouping, cost lenses), interaction design (compact lens tray, breadcrumb-ish active context), accessibility, and prototypes for handoff to ENG for implementation and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Compact Context Lens attached to left dock that shows: active workspace, pinned routes (max 5), active rollout flag, and cost-lens toggle
Session Jump keyboard shortcut opens a searchable palette with fuzzy matching across routes, models, and rollout tags
Context Lens maintains a persistent lightweight breadcrumb when collapsed and expands on hover or explicit toggle
Route grouping logic implemented in IA doc and agreed with PM/ENG (group by product > environment > model family)
Design prototype validated in 3 usability sessions with product/solutions engineers and meets baseline accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation checks
Figma prototype handed off with component tokens, states, and interaction specs and annotated PRD links
design_notes: We avoid a full sidebar rewrite; instead add a micro-surface (Context Lens) to reduce churn and preserve existing muscle memory for current heavy users.
Cost-lens concept is route-scoped: when enabled it annotates routes with per-route cost KPIs and surfaces an inline breakdown on hover.
Session Jump is separate from global command palette: it focuses on active-account resources and supports ephemeral session bookmarks.
Accessibility: ensure 4.5:1 contrast for icon badges in collapsed state and tabindex ordering for tray open/close and jump interactions.
Performance trade-off: prefer CSS-based transitions and DOM reuse over creating large new component trees to keep runtime cheap on low-end machines.
Telemetry: create a new interaction event group 'context_lens.*' to capture opens, selects, and cost-lens toggles for product analytics.
decisions: Use a left-dock micro-surface rather than a second-level persistent pane to reduce cognitive overhead
Limit pinned routes to 5 to avoid overflow complexity and encourage focused context
Fallback behavior: if the selected route is not available in the region, show 'compatible variant' with explicit callout (agreed with SRE)
Keyboard-first: prototype prioritizes fast keyboard navigation and supports command+K integration for Session Jump
